title: Phish brought near-record crowds to this Fenway dispensary — but not a product shortage
author: Samantha Genzer
bullets: New Dia Fenway saw sales and foot traffic match its record-setting 4/20 weekend during Phish's two concerts at Fenway Park.
Despite surging crowds, New Dia Fenway maintained inventory, hosting the Phish Phan Art marketplace benefiting the Mockingbird Foundation.
Fenway events including Phish and Tim McGraw attracted global visitors, with the dispensary prepared for high customer volume.

title: Red Sox homer 3 times over 7 pitches en route to statement sweep of Dodgers
author: Conor Ryan
bullets: The Boston Red Sox completed a three-game sweep of the LA Dodgers with an 8-4 win on Sunday.
Boston hit three home runs in seven pitches during the third inning, contributing to four homers in the game.
The Red Sox have won 28 of their last 33 games and hold the second AL Wild Card spot with a 60-51 record.

title: Rafaela homers for 3rd straight game as the Red Sox beat the Dodgers 8-4 for 3-game sweep
author: The Associated Press
bullets: Ceddanne Rafaela's homer marks his third consecutive game with a home run; Red Sox sweep Dodgers 8-4.
Red Sox's Jake Bennett allowed three runs over 5 2/3 innings, improving his record to 7-4.
Dodgers pitcher Emmet Sheehan gave up five runs in 2 2/3 innings; Red Sox scored two early runs.

title: Stoughton police chief and town manager placed on leave amid investigation after chief alleges discrimination, harrassment
author: Samantha Genzer
bullets: Stoughton Police Chief Donna McNamara and Town Manager Thomas Calter are on paid administrative leave amid harassment and discrimination investigations.
McNamara accuses Calter of discrimination, harassment, and interfering with her role, claiming he pressured her to resign.
The Stoughton Select Board initiated separate investigations and appointed temporary replacements for McNamara and Calter.

title: Here’s what meteorologists are saying about heavy rain and possible flooding Monday
author: Jack Pickell
bullets: Heavy rainfall and downpours expected in Boston could lead to flooding Monday, especially in poor drainage areas.
National Weather Service warns of isolated severe thunderstorms and damaging winds as a cold front approaches from the west.
Highest flooding risk is in interior Massachusetts, northwest Rhode Island, and much of Connecticut due to prior rainfalls.

title: Review & setlist: Phish soars over Fenway for two nights of rarities and redefined favorites
author: Perry Eaton
bullets: Phish performed two nights at Fenway Park, focusing on rarities and redefined favorites for fans.
The band delivered extended jams, including a rare cover of XTC's 'Melt the Guns', last played in 1987.
Setlists included a mix of classic hits and recent songs, showcasing Phish's improvisational skills.

title: Former Patriots 2024 2nd-round pick abruptly retires from NFL
author: Conor Ryan
bullets: Ja'Lynn Polk, a former Patriots second-round pick in 2024, retires from the NFL at 24 after two seasons.
Polk played only one season with the Patriots, struggling with 12 catches for 87 yards and two touchdowns in 2024.
New Orleans Saints placed Polk on the reserve/retired list; he missed recent practices due to personal reasons.

title: Mother of trooper killed in crash sues Saugus restaurant, alleging it over-served wrong-way driver
author: Samantha Genzer
bullets: Barbara Trainor filed a $20 million lawsuit against Tribu Mexican Kitchen & Bar in Saugus for allegedly over-serving alcohol.
The lawsuit claims Hernan Ramon Marrero was served nine drinks despite being visibly intoxicated before the fatal crash.
Essex County District Attorney's report found Marrero's blood alcohol level was 0.192, more than twice the legal limit.

title: Red Sox trade deadline live updates: Will Craig Breslow make another big move?
author: Conor Ryan
bullets: Red Sox acquired Curtis Mead from Nationals, but he is injured; further trades are likely before Monday's deadline.
Boston Red Sox linked to CJ Abrams, but acquiring him would require a significant trade package involving Franklin Arias.
Top rivals making moves: Yankees getting Luis Garcia Jr., Rays acquiring Freddy Peralta, while Red Sox pursue impact bats.

title: Man killed in East Boston overnight shooting
author: Samantha Genzer
bullets: A man was shot and killed near 464 Meridian St. in East Boston early Sunday morning.
The Boston Police Department has not made any arrests and is investigating the incident.
Authorities urge anyone with information about the shooting to contact BPD detectives at 617-343-4470.
